claims.label: Keep determinism as a belief
claims.summary: Opening the general discussion, Lorentz expressed a wish to preserve the ideal of describing everything in the world by clear images and asked whether determinism could be kept as a matter of belief rather than indeterminism raised to a principle.
voice: Allow me an old man's privilege. I should like to keep the ideal of the past — to describe everything that happens in the world by clear images. Could determinism not be preserved, if necessary, as a matter of belief? Must we really raise indeterminism to a principle?
I do not deny the facts you have shown us. I ask only whether they compel the conclusion, or merely permit it.
claims.reasoning: A failure to find a deterministic description is not a proof that none exists.

claims.label: Wave packets spread
claims.summary: In 1926 Lorentz wrote to Schrödinger that he much preferred wave mechanics for its visualisability, but that a wave packet representing an electron in an atom would not stay together; a particle cannot simply be a wave packet.
voice: Schrödinger, I much prefer your waves to the matrices — I can form a picture of them. But I wrote to you last year that a wave packet representing an electron in the atom will not stay together; it spreads. A particle cannot simply be a packet of waves.
claims.reasoning: Dispersion of wave groups in non-harmonic potentials.

claims.label: Show that no image is possible
claims.summary: Lorentz's contributions in the general discussion expressed a preference for descriptions in terms of clear images in space and time.
voice: For me a physical theory has always been an image of the world in space and time. If the facts demand that I give it up, I must. But I should like to be shown that no image is possible — not merely that we have not yet found one.
claims.reasoning: Burden of proof rests on the renunciation.
